lots.what_it_is: Mixed lot titled PLATED PIN DISH & RINGS INCL STERLING SILVER ETC: plated rectangular pin dish with an enamel R.M.S. STRATHAIRD (P&O) badge, five rings, a pentagram pendant, an identity plate engraved G.J. GARDNER LIEUT R.N.V.R. and a curb chain bracelet with tapered ends.

lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximum bids are 0. Buyer's premium 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198) would apply.
lots.confidence_reason: Items identified clearly and engravings read, but no hallmarks are visible, there is only one overall photo, and there are no price entries.
lots.dropped_entries: None: the researcher supplied no entries.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crops confirm the badge reads R.M.S. STRATHAIRD with a P&O house flag on a lifebuoy, and the plate reads G.J. GARDNER / LIEUT R.N.V.R. (the initials are partly worn). The identity plate has slots at each end, so it probably belongs with the curb chain as an identity bracelet. The dish looks plated and is worn and spotted. Rings: two pentagram or star signets, one textured band, one openwork band, one signet with a worn face. I could not see any hallmarks in the single photo.
lots.condition: Tarnished overall. The plating on the dish is worn and spotted. The rings and chain are worn from use.
lots.question_for_gowans: Which pieces are marked sterling (the rings, bracelet and identity plate)? What does the silver weigh in total? Does the G.J. Gardner RNVR plate attach to the curb chain as one identity bracelet, and does it carry any hallmark?

lots.what_it_is: Bag titled BAG OF SCRAP ITEMS INCL STERLING SILVER: chains, a bangle, rings, a spoon, a locket, a pierced buckle, a shield-shaped plate, a brooch, two egg-shaped pieces and a hallmarked bell (probably a baby rattle bell).
lots.guide_summary: No market evidence survives: the researcher found no entries and my own search was refused too (shared WebSearch budget used up). Guide 0 to 0. Value depends on the silver weight, which is not stated.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence and no weight, so both maximum bids are 0. Buyer's premium 19.8% would apply.
lots.confidence_reason: Several marks read clearly, but there are no price entries and no weight.
lots.dropped_entries: None: the researcher supplied no entries.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crops: the bell is marked A&S in a shaped cartouche, then a worn round mark (possibly the Birmingham anchor, not certain), a lion passant and a capital W. If that is Birmingham, W would be 1896, but the town mark is unconfirmed. The spoon is marked IC, a round sovereign-head duty mark, a lion passant and a capital N, which points to the Georgian or early Victorian period (no town mark visible). The brooch back is stamped STERLING. The plate's rectangular stamp is worn and reversed-looking, and I could not read it. The yellow chain and at least one ring look like base metal.
lots.condition: Scratched and worn, with tarnish. The rattle bell is complete as far as one photo shows. The mix includes costume pieces.
lots.question_for_gowans: What does the bag weigh in total, and how much of that is hallmarked sterling? Does the bell still have its whistle or handle? Is the town mark on the spoon visible?
